review_kind: static source and offline driver-structure review
status: complete with explicit experimental residual risks
scope: Per-controller original-workloop timers, lifecycle suspension and rebinding
Controller/ring/descriptor reference ownership and read-only mapping lifetime
Consumer hook cookies, in-flight readers, monotonic activity and real progress counters
Final gated observation, reservation ownership, explicit stop and retirement
Atomic runtime publication, status publication versus shutdown, and initialization failure cleanup
Bounded loaded text/constant sections, vtable target coverage and conservative first-return scan limits
verified_corrections: All three native role rings are required because the recognized dispatcher visits each without null guards.
Runtime readiness, running state, error pointer and routed-hook mask use explicit atomic access.
Management timer removal is conditional on successful event-source attachment.
Workloop candidates are retained under the lifecycle manager lock only after supported routes and no in-flight mutation are verified.
Workloop replacement drains reservations, removes the old timer and releases old references before attaching a replacement.
Explicit stop covers the temporary retiring state used during workloop replacement.
Status presence is checked under the same manager lock used when shutdown clears it.
Consumer completion updates the exact persistent counter cookie captured on entry; rebinding does not reset counters.

residual_risks.description: A downstream native completion callback may release the controller workloop gate. A foreign lifecycle caller that holds that gate while waiting for the original-call reservation could deadlock with the original call reacquiring the gate. The reviewed direct manual/dispatcher path does not establish safety for every downstream callback.
residual_risks.disposition: Experimental limitation documented in README; all callback and power-state lock interleavings have not been proved.

residual_risks.description: An already-running consumer that began before a new ring token was published cannot acquire the new counter cookie. If it advances a newly established baseline without another tracked consumption, the policy may conservatively keep rejecting that ring until later progress or rebinding.
residual_risks.disposition: Low-probability functional coverage limitation, especially for interrupt-side isochronous consumption; native driver locking remains responsible for safe consumption.

residual_risks.description: Static review does not establish 100 microsecond delivery, performance, sleep/wake stability, or safety on other machines and macOS driver implementations.
residual_risks.disposition: Requires actual testing; unknown private ABI or lifecycle overrides are rejected.

offline_cross_check.method: Compared base and MSI Interrupter vtable entries in extracted images; offline entries contain chained-fixup encodings, not runtime pointers.

not_claimed: No proof of the original MSI hardware fault or a universally safe workaround.
No claim that all Intel/AMD controller subclasses or all macOS builds are supported.
No claim that source review or offline tests substitute for hardware validation.

rechecked_paths: original-workloop candidate retained under lifecycle manager lock
explicit stop includes temporary retiring contexts
shared runtime-layout and hook-span helper integration
